notes:
Venture 0.21 — compass calibration you can trust, and a brightness control

• A calibration that the aircraft never heard used to sit on the screen for
  ever, showing a zero and "Waiting for the aircraft" with only CANCEL to
  press. START is now repeated until the aircraft answers, and the screen says
  which happened: no reply, refused, or accepted but sending no progress.
• The big number during a calibration is now the percentage, not the count of
  covered patches. The aircraft finishes on the percentage; it does not need
  all 80 patches filled, and turning the aircraft for the last few was work
  nobody needed to do. A good calibration on the bench finished at 72 of 80.
• The result now shows what the aircraft was calibrated to before, beside what
  this run would put there — offsets, scale and orientation — so you can see
  how far it moves before accepting it. ACCEPT is now SAVE.
• A save that does not reach the aircraft is reported instead of assumed. The
  old one sent once and said "saved" whether or not the aircraft heard, so a
  calibration could look written while the aircraft kept its old numbers.
  Venture now waits for the aircraft to confirm, then reads the values back off
  it and shows what it is actually holding.
• After saving, REBOOT restarts the aircraft from the same screen. The new
  offsets are live as soon as they are saved, but the aircraft's navigation is
  still working from the old ones until it restarts.
• Screen brightness: Configuration > Controller > SCREEN. Ten steps, and the
  screen follows the slider as you move it. Dim it to save the controller's
  battery on a long survey, or run it bright in sun. It stays where you put it
  across restarts.
• The controller no longer claims an aircraft that has stopped talking. If the
  flight controller goes quiet while the rest of the aircraft keeps
  transmitting, FLY and COMPASS now grey out as they should, instead of
  offering a link with nothing behind it.
